chunks: Mu'awiyah ibn 'Ammar narrated from Abū 'Abdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

The one who was in charge of the sacrificial camels of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله was Nājiyah ibn Jundab al-Khuzā'ī al-Aslamī. The one who shaved his head صلى الله عليه وآله on the day of al-Hudaybiyah was Khirāsh ibn Umayyah al-Khuzā'ī, and the one who shaved his head during his hajj was Ma'mar ibn 'Abdillāh ibn Hārith ibn Naṣr ibn 'Awf ibn 'Awīj ibn 'Adiyy ibn Ka'b. It was said to him while he was shaving him: 'O Ma'mar, the ear of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله is in your hand.' He said: 'By Allah, I indeed count it as a tremendous favor upon me from Allah.' Ma'mar ibn 'Abdillāh used to comb his hair صلى الله عليه وآله, and the two garments of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله in which he entered ihram were two Yemeni garments, 'Ibrī and Ẓafār. And he stopped the talbiyah when the sun declined on the Day of 'Arafah.

key_terms.أَحْرَمَ: entered the state of ihram for hajj
key_terms.التَّلْبِيَةَ: the pilgrimage invocation recited during ihram
key_terms.الْحُدَيْبِيَةِ: the well-known location and event where the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله halted and later had his head shaved
key_terms.بُدْنِ: the sacrificial camels offered in hajj
key_terms.حَجَّتِهِ: his pilgrimage, referring here to the Prophet’s صلى الله عليه وآله hajj
key_terms.عَرَفَةَ: the Day and place of 'Arafah during hajj rites
key_terms.يُرَجِّلُ: used to comb and arrange the hair

ai.seo_question: Who shaved the Prophet’s صلى الله عليه وآله head during Hudaybiyah and during his hajj, and when did he stop the talbiyah?
ai.summary: This hadith records specific details about the Prophet’s صلى الله عليه وآله hajj, including those who tended his sacrificial camels, shaved his head, and arranged his hair. It also preserves details of his ihram garments and the time when he ceased the talbiyah on the Day of 'Arafah, making it important for both historical knowledge and the sunnah of hajj.
